steps.name: Plain-Dressed Bard
steps.text: History records that out of a sense the war between the Draco and Aslan had become far too protracted and bitter, the final King Gaeil signed a peace treaty.

steps.name: Plain-Dressed Bard
steps.text: Legends say he opted to melt down his soldiers' weapons as a sign of his determination, but his subjects could hardly accept such a defeat. Thus they conspired to revolt, and assassinated the monarch.

steps.name: Plain-Dressed Bard
steps.text: But just as you've referenced in many a speech, a single assassination is not enough to extinguish the Red Dragon's whole bloodline.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: No matter how the Victorians write the history books, they cannot change what facts we've seen with our own eyes.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: The Aslan promised to share Victoria's kingship with the Draco, yet didn't hand over the crown for nearly a century.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: With the lions' ambitions so conspicuous to this point, I wonder. Six blade marks stabbed King Gaeil through. How many of them were by Aslan hands?

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: Not to mention the Draco king fleeing the royal capital after, fate unknown. And the Kingdom of Tara without its ruler was subjugated under Victorian sovereign authority, as if a matter of course.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: I presume it wasn't his own subjects who prevented the Draco's return to the city.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: This is why I very much enjoy your works based on the Tarans' own ballads. You've led the people to see more of history's truth.

steps.name: Plain-Dressed Bard
steps.text: Thank you for your appreciation.

steps.name: Plain-Dressed Bard
steps.text: To write this story, I saw plays performed in the country, and paid a visit to some wandering minstrels who'd inherited the Taran tradition.

steps.name: Plain-Dressed Bard
steps.text: —But what struck me most wasn't the endangerment of Taran culture. It was how so many lives were just slipping away.

steps.name: Plain-Dressed Bard
steps.text: Perhaps you believe the Tarans' ideal nation, and a border with Victoria, are necessary for the Taran people to be saved.

steps.name: Plain-Dressed Bard
steps.text: But I think, if we ourselves can live better, if we can plant seeds of ideas for the many Tarans who can't read...

steps.name: Plain-Dressed Bard
steps.text: Won't we have won then and there, against the Victorians who want us trapped in ignorance and poverty all our lives?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: You want to bring that lot with you? Don't even think about it.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: If you'll wait until they rest, if you'll share your own food with them, that I can accept.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: But we've avoided the patrol out of pure luck the last two days. What if we don't the next time? Those kids must be seven or eight. Can't fight back with weapons, can't run fast enough. What do you do about that?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I can fight... I'll protect them.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: You want to cross through the uninhabited region, to completely escape Trent's jurisdiction. I can aid you, the whole way.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I contacted the organization I belong to, with the help of Bagpipe and Ch'en... my colleagues. I've confirmed the closest safehouse—is just along this way.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: If all we need is some tents, and a small amount of emergency supplies for the countryside, they can transport it over without a problem.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: And I know, the territory over there... belongs to a well-hearted Duke. Once we're there, the army won't be after you anymore, at the very least.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Really? There's an honest-to-God noble who'd smile on people like us?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: He has... reason to shelter the Tarans.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: And how do you know?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...Before long, perhaps we'll all know.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: We'll have ways to survive, bringing those people along.

steps.name: Overwrought Taran Refugee
steps.text: But. Don't forget. They're Infected.

steps.name: Overwrought Taran Refugee
steps.text: We've constantly been scarpering with our lives. What are we doing inviting death to our sides?

steps.name: Overwrought Taran Refugee
steps.text: And we don't know when the sick'll have their flare-ups. Or when they'll just kick the bucket outright...

steps.name: Overwrought Taran Refugee
steps.text: What's the point in you saving these sorts of people?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I don't know.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I only know, that when someone saved me... I wanted to ask her the same. Why?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Even though I was... so close to death.

steps.name: Overwrought Taran Refugee
steps.text: What are you getting at?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I'm an Infected too.

steps.name: Overwrought Taran Refugee
steps.text: Wha? Oh. Er...

steps.name: Overwrought Taran Refugee
steps.text: *cough*. Alright. Doesn't mean much to be Infected. Wouldn't have lived much longer than Infected ourselves without your help anyway. Haha.

steps.name: Overwrought Taran Refugee
steps.text: Still...

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Oripathy won't spread just because we're in the same place.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: It's okay. You can keep a bit of distance, if you're scared. I don't mind.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: But take those Infected with you on your escape... Trust me.

steps.name: Overwrought Taran Refugee
steps.text: ...Fine. I trust you! Selmon. You heard what she said...

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: —I'm not fleeing.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: If you're gonna take the ones that can't fight, take 'em. Suit your own self.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: But my aim isn't gonna change one bit. I'm returning to Dublinn.

steps.name: Solemn Officer
steps.text: ...These two units have gone unaccounted for a week by now. We may surmise these circumstances relate to Dublinn, being similar to past spectre force incidents.

steps.name: Biting Officer
steps.text: Similar? No, the situation we're looking at now is completely unalike.

steps.name: Biting Officer
steps.text: These rebels previously would muster a single armed force to surface somewhere, launch an attack, and that was it.

steps.name: Biting Officer
steps.text: Now, violence which we suspect to be Dublinn-incited is blanketing every corner of southern Victoria.

steps.name: Solemn Officer
steps.text: ...Is the Marquess of Trent sticking fast to his orders?

steps.name: Biting Officer
steps.text: Obviously. No matter the volume of suspicious circumstances reported outside nomadic cities, we must have CLARITY on them. Get this entire region's state of affairs under control.

steps.name: Solemn Officer
steps.text: But of all the small-scale conflicts, only the arson at Redridge seems truly suspect, and there was no follow-up on the fire there either.

steps.name: Solemn Officer
steps.text: Maybe we should set these particular dossiers aside for now? Or should we leave them?

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: Please lend said dossiers to me, officers.

steps.name: Solemn Officer
steps.text: You're... j...

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: And refrain with the greetings.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: Also, just as before, no need to make a record of access to these dossiers.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: This arson... may be worth a deeper investigation.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Have a sip of water, ould Breandán. I picked some berries too. This place can't be too far from a settlement, what with a grove this thick.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: You want some berries too, Holly? Alright, you eat those, and then you walk on your own two legs this afternoon. Won't need anyone else carrying you, okay?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: How about you, Moran? Wait, you don't eat stuff this sweet, do you...

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: ...Thank you.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: ...*sigh*.

steps.name: Tempersome Taran Refugee
steps.text: Hey, how long are we stopping here for?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: While Bagpipe and Ch'en are fetching things for us. We're all knackered as is, anyhow. Got a chance to catch our breaths.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Don't worry, I guarantee we'll find the closest village before lights-out.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: We're far enough from all the trouble we made anyhow. If we hang around here and hole up for a few days, we oughtn't get caught.

steps.name: Tempersome Taran Refugee
steps.text: Fine, pick me some berries too. First time seeing you happy in days.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Er, really? I've just been glad Reed's so reliable, and her two friends too. Kind souls, plus they can fight.

steps.name: Tempersome Taran Refugee
steps.text: You sure? It's not just how your days of suffering are almost at an end?

steps.name: Tempersome Taran Refugee
steps.text: We're going to keep pushing into the wastes, find Dublinn and join them. You, though, I bet you'd prefer to stay behind in village life.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: ...Er, I can't say that for sure.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: I... *sigh* I just can't get over you lot doing things this way.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: We were all happy just with escaping at first, the further the better. That was before we ran into Selmon.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: She only got to persuade you all to join Dublinn once stuff got tougher on us.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: None of you've... even seen a real Dublinn army, have you?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Are you still thinking about Reed?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: She contacted Rhodes Island in full view of us after borrowing our comms equipment. Getting supplies has been smooth too. All signs indicate she's not out to trick us.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Haha, I'm not suspectin' her as much, I'm just a little concerned... Did she really make a recovery?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Granted, she's a Vouivre, but I'm still a little surprised at all the life in her... She gave my hands a right shock swingin' at me before we recognized each other.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Suppose that's a good thing, though. Just, I can't shake the feelin' there's weight on her mind. Whatever it is, she wants to do it, but it seems to hurt her so much.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Plus...

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Plus what?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: The way she fights just seems somehow familiar.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Did I meet her, even before Outcast brought her in, back at County Hillock?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Oh, aye, there you are, Reed! Perfect, me and Chenchen've been talkin'...

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: ...We're talking about which way we're heading. This route happens to take us to a nearby settlement.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: No, we can't—keep going in this direction... I'll tell the others—to stop.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Are you sayin'...

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Chenchen, on your nine!
The cavalry saber concealed in the bushes snaps in two.
The one holding it doesn't shift an inch. Ch'en is sure her slash didn't harm anyone, but out from under the bush is still a hint of spilled blood. Blood deep and dark, old and dry.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Is this... dead patrol?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: No, they're from the barracks. There's more over there.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Traces of bolts, sabers... and Arts.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: This battle probably happened a week ago. This barracks unit was ambushed, and slaughtered to a man.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Who was the enemy, then? How come they didn't leave a single corpse behind?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: They've... left.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: They've all left? But with a battle this fierce, both sides should've taken equal damages, right?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Bagpipe, remember the group of soldiers we discovered before encountering Reed?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Mm... they had uncanny Arts planted in them, eyes full of fire...

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Reed, you were in County Hillock too. Didn't you see soldiers like that?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...Yes, I know of them.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: They're... parted souls.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Those with the misfortune of being deceased, yet unable to rest...

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: You're not sayin'—the ones who killed these soldiers are dead themselves, and they're still marchin' even after?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: The traces of firefights we were chasin' before, it resembles those too.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: ...It's the only possibility.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Chenchen, I don't know what your thoughts are, but I... I can't quite accept it, if that's what this is.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: What kind of person would—keep on controllin' them, even after they're dead? That's just far too cruel.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...Selmon?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Like hell they're dead. You're all howling up the wrong tree.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: But we saw, with our own eyes...

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: You saw something somewhere else. I only believe what I see myself.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Dublinn defeated a Victorian unit. They won, moved onto the next place, and now they're prepping to save more Tarans.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: You know I'm gonna...

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...Are you worried about something?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Don't act like my da.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: If Fionn's lot want to go with you, suit their own selves, but I know you're not in with us. It's those two Vouivre you're with.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: You just want to settle us someplace, ensure we're not going to die today. You'll make us live the same old life Victoria had for us, not knowing if we'll see tomorrow.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: And after that, you'll abandon us.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Am I not right, 'Leader'?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: No. No, don't call me that...

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Right. 'No.' Single word I've heard most from you so far.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: I'm heading off now, going the way you didn't want us to go. It's only war and death, isn't it? Like the Tarans haven't seen plenty of both?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: I don't want to hear an outsider tell me 'no' ever again.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: I know she's fumin', but truth is, it's not you who's pissin' her off.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: So, are you... um, are you alright?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I want to go with her.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: There might still be... unexploded mines, and lingering Arts, left on the battlefield. It'll be dangerous to keep—going that way.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Can you call the rest over for me?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Didn't you want these Tarans to steer clear of the battlefield?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Mm.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: But—Selmon says, it's their choice.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: And I... I promised, I'd escort them, until...

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Until I'm no longer needed.
